note: Conventional project-Memory keys the customer can pre-fill. Each carries a description that is passed to the dev agent (key + description + value) so it has proper context. `is_secret` pre-checks the hidden toggle.

placeholders.description: GitHub personal access token (or fine-grained token) with repo scope. Used by the agent to read/create branches, open pull requests and read issues on the project's GitHub repository.
GitLab personal/project access token with api + write_repository scope. Used to push branches, open merge requests and read CI results on the project's GitLab repository.
AWS access key ID (public part of the IAM credentials). Identifies the AWS account/role used to inspect target infrastructure.
AWS secret access key (paired with AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID). Grants AWS API access; used read-only to describe/plan, never to apply changes.
Default AWS region (e.g. eu-west-1) the target resources are deployed in.
Full GCP service-account key JSON. Authenticates gcloud/Google client libraries; the agent uses it read-only to inspect the target GCP project.
Google Cloud project ID the resources belong to.
Base URL of the Supabase project (https://<ref>.supabase.co). The frontend/backend connects to this endpoint for auth and data.
Supabase anonymous/public API key used by the client SDK to reach the project with row-level-security enforced.
Supabase service-role key (bypasses row-level security). Only for trusted server-side use; handle with care.
Full database connection string (postgres://user:pass@host:port/db). The app reads/writes persistent data through it.
Token/password to authenticate against the container registry where images are pushed/pulled.
API key for an OpenAI-compatible endpoint the built application should call at runtime (distinct from the platform's own build model).
SMTP connection string (smtp://user:pass@host:port) the application uses to send transactional email.
Stripe secret API key (sk_...) the application uses server-side for payments. Use a test key for non-production builds.
